spine_carrier.py module: the requirement spine's registry CARRIER (OI-12 / repo-lock D-5). SPINE_TABLE maps an id column to its TOML tier table (SR-ID->requirement, LLR-ID->design, TC-ID->test); SPINE_COLUMN maps a carrier key to today's COLUMN NAME and is the exact inverse of migrate_carrier.KEY. rows_from_text(text, id_col, carrier) -> {id: row} under today's column names, or None when a TOML text does not parse (absent, never empty); rows_from_toml / rows_from_csv are the two arms. carriers(rel) -> both suffixed paths, for an applicability test that must span the cutover. resolve(path) -> the live carrier file, RAISING when both exist rather than resolving by precedence; load(path, id_col) -> rows in file order, the shape csv.DictReader returns, raising on a carrier that exists and will not parse. The `-000` example filter is NOT applied here - that is trace_text's rule.
Notes: source - spine_carrier consumes nothing by design, the trace_text pattern: text in, rows out, with resolve()'s existence check the single deliberate exception because the dual-home refusal must have one home. ONE module rather than eleven copies is an owner ruling (2026-08-10, repo-lock D-6) that AMENDS the F5 rejection of a shared _kitcommon: F5 buys cross-script copy-ability and was written for small stable plumbing, but a duplicated VOCABULARY fails silently rather than visibly. CLI: --check converts in memory and verifies the round-trip, writing nothing, exit 1 with a finding naming the registry, row id and field for each cell that did not survive; without --check it writes each .toml beside its source and STILL refuses on a lossy result. KEY is the column -> carrier-key map and the definition of record; spine_carrier.SPINE_COLUMN is its inverse, pinned by test_rule_sync.
